issues.description: The problem statement requires Bookstore to be initialized with an array of Book (init(books: [Book])), but the solution implements an initializer taking a Set<Book> (init(books: Set<Book>)) and assigns it to a property declared as [Book]. This creates a type/signature mismatch (and an assignment error) and is incompatible with the client code in the solution which passes a [Book].
issues.suggestedFix: Make the initializer signature consistent with the problem statement and the rest of the code. Change the Bookstore initializer in the solution to init(books: [Book]) and assign the parameter directly to the books property (let books: [Book]). Alternatively, if Set<Book> is intended, update the problem statement and client usage to require and pass a Set<Book> and adjust the books property type accordingly. The simplest fix: replace init(books: Set<Book>) with init(books: [Book]).

issues.description: The problem statement requires Bookstore to provide an initializer with signature init(books: [Book]) (an array of Book). The reference solution implements init(books: Set<Book>) (a Set of Book). Although the parameter name 'books' matches, the differing parameter type creates a mismatch between the stated API in the exercise and the provided solution implementation, which can confuse students about the expected initializer signature and the collection type to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the initializer signatures consistent. Change the solution's initializer to match the problem statement: init(books: [Book]) { self.books = books }. Alternatively, if a Set is intentional, update the problem statement and template to require init(books: Set<Book>) so all artifacts use the same collection type.
